summary: Physically preallocate and lock dedicated VM RAM with libvirt. API impact: existing contract; Core enforces VMCreateSpec.memory through vm-create/vm-update, retains vm-power outcomes and inventory adoption. Older definitions need a stopped save.

guide.reason: Explain running physical reservation versus stopped capacity commitment, Core upgrade and stopped-save steps, overhead and failure recovery.

api.reason: Existing fields and auth/retry contracts; document native enforcement and existing definition/Core compatibility.

roadmap.reason: Correct an implemented memory mode; no milestone scope or acceptance status changes.

state.reason: Dedicated memory is enforced by the host, with no Controller-owned reservation state.
state.record: Pool master managed-journal VMCreateSpec.memory plus persistent libvirt domain backing. Inventory.managed.vms reports the same UUID/mode/size for fresh Controller adoption; no rewrite or interruption of running guests.

verification.method: Focused red/green regression, Go race suites, native disposable libvirt RAM/locking/failure checks, API checks and simulated Chromium copy/layout review; see report for actual results and untested limits.
